You know there was a quote from Larry Page, the Google CEO. Page said he'd rather donate his money to people like Elon Musk than charity. At the time, this was just a few years ago, this angered me. It just seemed like an example of big business being completely out of touch with the needs of the people and society. Then I started to research Musk, and today - I'd be inclined to agree with Page!

Musk has really showed how much our capitalist society has broken down. What he's doing in the rocket industry we could have been doing decades ago. The only reason we weren't is because companies like Lockheed and Boeing are now controlled by shareholders and run by marketing and business types. Their goal in life begins and ends with money. They have no big picture for society or anything like that. Their big picture is making more money and buying more yachts. Musk on the other hand looks at things from the perspective of what could we do to improve the world. And he is in the paradoxically rare situation of not only being brilliant, but also a billionaire - allowing him to actually bring his ideas, where he has enough time, to life. On the ideas he does not have enough time, such as the hyper rail, he does all he can to help others bring them to life as he is driven not by profit, but by progress!

The things Musk is aiming for will completely revolutionize our entire species. For instance he wants to colonize Mars. This doesn't mean having a few dozen scientists digging through the dirt searching for microbes or whatever. He wants hundreds of thousands of people on the planet starting an entirely parallel civilization. And this would is obviously just the beginning. This is not only enormous for the future of humanity (our planet has already gone through multiple mass extinctions) but also even basic economics should we get back to the penny pinchers. Asteroid mining, interplanetary travel and service, and the -you know- whole thing about building an entirely new civilization from scratch.

Anyhow, I could go on but I don't know. It feels strange to answer your rhetorical question this way but to a degree, and at least in terms of the current state of society, I'd say - yeah, he is.
